title: Clarinet eval deltas and decision brief (Q3 2026)
content:
Purpose:
This doc summarizes the Clarinet model family onboarding sweep (v3 variants) against our standard production prompt sets and the lightweight adversarial probes we deployed last sprint. Objective: pick a single v3.x candidate to promote to staging for Dedicated trials, or record a clear reject with rollback-linked criteria.

High-level takeaways (TL;DR):
- v3.2 (int8 qkv-split) shows a consistent 8-12% latency win and a 3.7% token-cost reduction versus baseline v3.0, with very small quality regressions on edge long-form synthesis prompts.
- v3.3 (fused-attn kernels + prefix-cache tweak) improves coherence on multi-turn prompts (win +6.4% on convo-recall metric) but regresses on factual answer accuracy on our short-answer bank (loss -2.9%).
- v3.1-beta (RLHF fine-tune) has the best subjective safety/toxicity profile but increases median p95 latency by ~18ms under burst QPS.
- Recommendation: promote v3.2 to staging with a guarded canary (5% traffic) and tight rollback triggers (detailed below). v3.3 to remain as an experimental branch until we isolate factual regression cause.

Test matrix (subset shown):
- Prompt pools: product-help (500 prompts), code-assist (300), long-form-edit (150), short-fact (400), adversarial-toxicity (200).
- Metrics: ROUGE-L, BLEU (code), convo-recall (custom), factual-F1 (entity extraction), toxicity-reduction (tox), latency-ms (p50/p95), cost-per-1k-tokens.
- Environment: Dedicated-stub infra (A100-80GB equiv), batch size=dynamic, caching=on for long-form tests, sampling temp=0.2 for short-fact, temp=0.7 for open generation.

ASCII leaderboard snapshot (aggregated normalized score, higher better):
Model         | PctDeltaScore | p95-latency-ms | Factual-F1 | Toxicity | Notes
--------------|---------------|----------------|------------|----------|-------------------------------
v3.0 (base)   | 0.00          | 142            | 0.872      | 0.016    | baseline
v3.1-beta     | +1.9          | 160            | 0.881      | 0.008    | safer, slower
v3.2          | +7.4          | 129            | 0.858      | 0.015    | best perf/cost
v3.3          | +3.2          | 136            | 0.848      | 0.014    | better convo recall

Win/loss (pairwise quick notes):
- v3.2 vs v3.0: wins on latency and cost, loses small on long-form coherence (human eval delta -1.6 pts).
- v3.3 vs v3.0: wins on convo-recall and stability for prefixed prompts, loses on short-fact accuracy where entity hallucinations crept up.
- v3.1-beta vs v3.0: wins on safety/toxicity; loses on throughput and cold-start latency.

Representative regression cases (examples included so SRE & product can triage):
1) Long-form synthesis prompt (product-help): input: "Draft a two-page onboarding doc for new data scientists at a fintech firm."
   - v3.0: coherent structure, correct headings.
   - v3.2: repeats section intros, tangential paragraphs after 3rd token block, hallucinated API names in paragraph 2.
   - Fix hypothesis: int8 qkv rounding affects long-range attention normalization; further ablation needed with higher precision KV cache for long sequences.

2) Short-fact bank (single-shot): Q: "Who authored the paper on sparse attention in 2020?"
   - v3.3: answers with a wrong author (confuses first author with a coauthor).
   - Hypothesis: fused-attn microkernel reorders positional bias slightly; run targeted unit tests for positional encodings.

Operational impact and rollout plan:
- Canary plan for v3.2: 5% traffic on staging Dedicated pool for 72 hours, monitor these signals: 
  - user-visible error rate > 0.5% (5xx or timeout) -> rollback
  - factual-F1 drop > 2% on sampled short-fact set -> rollback
  - p95 latency increase > 12% vs baseline -> pause canary
  - sustained CPU/GPU mem increase > 10% -> investigate.

Quality gating checklist (must pass to graduate from staging to broader Dedicated):
- Automated evals: no metric regression > 1.5% on primary buckets (short-fact, product-help).
- Human eval: side-by-side preference >= 48% vs baseline on long-form set (n=200).
- Ops sanity: memory and latency within SLA; cold-start not exceeding 50ms over baseline p50.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- A) Run int8-with-high-precision-kv ablation (Aisha) by 2026-07-23.
- B) Add 250 adversarial fact probes targeted at authorship/date confusion patterns (Tomás).
- C) Re-run v3.3 with disabled fused-attn micro-ops to confirm positional bias theory (Benjy).
- D) Draft customer-facing note if we promote v3.2 explaining "minor long-form tradeoff" and mitigation plan (owner: Maya).

Decision rationale (short):
We prioritize predictable unit economics and lower latency for Dedicated customers. v3.2 gives measurable cost & latency benefits with small, explainable regressions that are mitigable via targeted precision ablations and prompt guardrails (short-term). v3.3 is promising for convo products but needs more work on factual consistency. v3.1-beta remains a safety branch we should keep for products with extra toxicity constraints.

Appendix: quick metric definitions and links:
- convo-recall: fraction of context entities present in 2-turn continuation.
- factual-F1: strict token-match F1 over curated short-fact bank.
- toxicity-reduction: measured via internal classifier calibrated on community data.

Linked PRs / experiments:
- PR: github.com/redwood/clarinet-models/pull/317 -> implementation of qkv-split int8
- Experiment: infra/experiment/clarinet-canary-0720 (monitoring dashboards linked in Confluence page above)

If you disagree with the recommendation or want to surface other regressions, add inline comments in this doc and ping leads.

-- Maya (eng-applied-ml)
